_readme: THE NINETEEN WORDS THE PRODUCT IS MADE OF, ONE LINE EACH.
Authored by the kit: Presentation/MetricGlossary.swift. The welcome screen selects four
of them (WelcomeGuide.highlights), /help/#numbers carries all nineteen, and the app's
own "What the numbers mean" topic renders the same rows.
These are index lines, not the reference page: the thresholds, the outcome ladder and
the 70 % score stay in HelpCatalog, which has no equivalent on the site.
AN ENTRY IS NINE FIELDS, because four surfaces, two stores and one lint read it:
id         a slug that outlives a rewording
term       THE LABEL — the iPhone card, the web tile, /help/'s <dt>
short      the same word at the watch's width: AT MOST SEVEN CHARACTERS wherever
`surfaces` names "watch". A MIP cell is about seven, and three watch
labels shipped over it. The budget is a field rather than an exemption,
so it fails a test instead of failing a rider.
expansion  what the phone and the web append after " · ": "clean jibes per hour".
Empty where the term is already the whole of it.
line       the one sentence — THE RULE
sentence   the clause the two store descriptions print instead of the label
surfaces   who may DEMAND this word: ios | watch | web | appstore | ciq
places     WHERE IT SHOWS, concretely: watchPage | fitField | connectField |
phoneRow | phonePage | card | web | help. Rendered into the one line the
help topic prints under the rule, so a rider comparing two screens is
pointed at both.
labels     EVERY SPELLING a surface may print for this term. GlossaryLintTests
fails on a rider-facing metric label that is in no entry's labels and on
no allow-list.
fit        the FIT developer field behind it, or "" (docs/fit-schema.md).
EIGHT ENTRIES WERE ADDED ON 20 SEPTEMBER 2026 — the verdict words. A tester compared
three screens about one afternoon and read "Turn success 29 %" in Garmin Connect,
"93 % flew through" on the site and 44 % on the phone. Three measurements, two of them
sharing a word the rider is never supposed to see. flewThrough, clean, speedKept, dry,
touchdown, fellIn, takeoffs and takeoffAttempts each have their own row now.
`id`, `term`, `expansion`, `line`, `surfaces`, `places`, `labels` and `fit` are
kit-owned: regenerate with COPY_WRITE=1 swift test --filter CopyContractTests. `short`
and `sentence` are HAND-AUTHORED here, the way `lexicon` and `ciqListingTitle` are in
phrases.json — a regeneration carries them forward and seeds only a brand-new entry
from the kit.

entries.line: How much of your session you spent flying rather than just moving.
entries.sentence: how much of it you spent on the foil

entries.line: One takeoff starts a flight. A touchdown or a swim ends it. Both are counted.
Every turn gets one: flew through, touchdown, or fell in.
entries.sentence: whether you flew through it, touched down, or fell in

entries.line: How many jibes in a row you stayed out of the water, and the best run of the day.
entries.sentence: your longest run of jibes without falling in

entries.line: Dry jibes per hour. Falling in more often cannot raise it.
Clean jibes per hour. Clean: flew through, held your speed, and 10 quiet seconds after.
Turns per hour, every counted turn and not only the jibes. It stands in for JPH on a session whose wind axis named no jibes.
Swims per hour. Nobody wants it high, and it counts every fall.
Your fastest 2 seconds, 10 seconds, 500 m and nautical mile. The speedsurfing world uses the same windows.
The mean of your best five separate 10-second runs. They may not overlap, so one lucky reach cannot carry it.
Your fastest 500 m that ends within 50 m of where it started. It contains a jibe, so it measures the turn as well as the speed.
entries.sentence: your fastest 500 m that comes back to where it started

entries.line: The turn kept the foil, from the sweep until you were flying again.
A jibe that flew through, held 70 % of its entry speed, and stayed quiet for 10 s.
entries.sentence: which of your jibes were clean

entries.line: The share of counted turns that held 70 % of their entry speed and never dropped off the foil.
entries.sentence: how many of your turns held their speed

entries.line: You did not fall in. A touchdown still counts as dry.
entries.sentence: the jibes you did not swim out of

entries.line: The foil went in and you kept going. Dry, and not clean.
Every time you ended up in the water, in a turn or in a straight line.
How many times you got up on the foil. One takeoff starts every flight.
Every pumping burst, whether you got up or not. Attempts are takeoffs plus failed attempts.
entries.sentence: how often you pumped, including the times you did not get up
